items.title: Earl Turbinton Interview, 1990-09-01
items.q: And all of our mentors were sort of doing other projects. I think Alvin had gone to start his program at Southern, so we weren't hearing much of him here. Ellis was off with his other projects

ctx.x: Can you address a little bit about what do you think the forces were that led to the closure? I mean, I know you said there were lots of other problems, but were there any other things that you think led to the closure?

Just economics. Had we been able to sustain ourselves as well? See, that was a period, as I said, where, say, from 64 up to that period, even for New Orleans, I mean, this was a period that we were making upward of, say, $350 to $500 a week per person and better sometimes, which is, many times musicians don't make, on a local level, they aren't doing it well here now in the 90s or late 80s that wasn't happening. The group was very popular. We were able to get some very good bookings, and we were recognized as…
And the workshop did bear fruit. The workshop did bear fruit.

items.title: Ellis Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: alto saxophone player called me, named Earl Turbinton. I got two or three jobs because Earl either didn’t show up, or whatever.

ctx.x: Yeah. L-u and Charlie’s. The way I happened to get that job, alto saxophone player called me, named Earl Turbinton. I got two or three jobs because Earl either didn’t show up, or whatever. But at Lu and Charlie’s, Earl didn’t show up, and Charlie said, “Man, can you put a band together?” I said yeah. So I put this band together with James

Black and John [?Br] – because [Br?] had been playing with me at the theater gigs, a trumpet player, at the theater gigs – and Ralph Johnson. We had an assortment of bass players. There were just all kinds of bass players. The last one that I remember was a guy named [?] Johnson. All of them except one, I think, was electric bass. I stayed there until everything started to get stale, because nobody – James was writing, but James was writing some different kind of music at the time. My plate was getting full, just…
